scope.flow: cancelDepositRequest removal from activeDepositRequesters and unregisterVault safety check
scope.environment: deposit request management and vault unregistration in a DeFi protocol

statements.text: A user has claimableDepositAssets greater than 0, a claimable deposit liability from funds processed by the Investment Manager but not yet claimed via deposit().
activeDepositRequesters correctly includes the user while the claimable liability exists.
The user initiates and then cancels a second pending deposit request.
cancelDepositRequest resolves the second pending request and unconditionally removes the user from activeDepositRequesters.
The Owner calls unregisterVault, deregistering the vault.
cancelDepositRequest's removal logic fails to account for a still-existing claimable deposit liability, so the set removal occurs despite the outstanding liability.
After the cancellation the user still holds claimableDepositAssets greater than 0, but activeDepositRequestersCount is forced to 0 instead of the expected 1.
unregisterVault's metrics.activeDepositRequestersCount == 0 check is bypassed by the falsely zero counter, allowing the vault to be deregistered while 1000 tokens/shares remain owed.

activeDepositRequestersCount should equal 1 while the user has claimableDepositAssets greater than 0, so that unregisterVault's activeDepositRequestersCount == 0 check only succeeds when no user liabilities remain.
The proof-of-concept shows the user can still claim their funds after unregistration by calling deposit().

ambiguities: Report does not state that anyone can call cancelDepositRequest or unregisterVault; authorization is not specified for either call.
Whether the second request was funded or how Liability 2 arose before cancellation is not described.
The exact time/order relation between the second request, its cancellation, and any deposit() claim is not fully specified.
Whether an actual on-chain unregistration with outstanding 1000 tokens/shares occurred or only a proof-of-concept is asserted.
The mechanism by which an unregistered vault could be replaced with a malicious implementation is not described.
